sentences.text: For the reasons mentioned in the application, which is supported by an affidavit, application is allowed and delay in filing the appeal (M.A.No. 5233/2019) is hereby condoned, appeal was admitted and with the consent of parties, both the appeals were heard finally.

3. This order shall govern disposal of M.A.No. 797/2014 and M.A.No. 5233/2019 as both these appeals are filed against the common award dated 16/5/2014 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior in Claim Case No. 73/2012; whereby, claimants have been awarded a compensation of Rs. 3,42,000/- alongwith interest @7% per annum for death of their son Farhan Qureshi in road accident dated 27/10/2011 and liability for payment of compensation amount was fastened over driver/owner and Insurance Company jointly and severally.
4.

Briefly stated facts of the case are that on 27/10/2011 when deceased Farhan Qureshi, aged 19 years was returning back from Jorasi Temple alongwith his friend Akash on a motorcycle, it is alleged that due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Vehicle No. MP07GA1328, it dashed the motorcycle, due to which deceased sustained grievous hurts and succumbed to the same.

Therefore,
claimants/parents have filed a claim case before the Claims Tribunal under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking total compensation of Rs. 15,50,000/-; however, by the impugned award, the claimants have been awarded a compensation as mentioned hereinabove.
5. M.A.No. 797/2014 has been filed on behalf of claimants seeking enhancement in the compensation amount.
Accordingly to them, Claims Tribunal erred in assessing the income of deceased at Rs. 4,000/- per month, whereas, he used to earn Rs. 5,500/- per month.

It is further submitted that learned Claims Tribunal erred in applying the multiplier of 13 as per the age of mother of deceased; whereas, multiplier has to be used as per the deceased in light of latest decisions of Apex Court.
Further no amount has been awarded under the head future prospects.

6. M.A.No. 5233/2019 has been filed on behalf of Insurance Company stating that on the date of accident, offending vehicle did not possessing fitness certificate as is clear from para 11 of the impugned award and therefore, learned Claims Tribunal erred in fastening the liability over the Insurance Company.

In support of his submissions, he relied upon decision of this Court in the matter of United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Vinod and Ors., 2020ACJ2641.
7.

entities.text: United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Vinod and Ors., 2020ACJ2641
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the parties at length and perused the record.

8. As regards M.A.No. 797/2014, in absence of any documentary evidence, in the opinion of this Court, learned Claims Tribunal did not err in assessing the income of deceased at Rs. 4,000/- per month; however, erred in applying the multiplier of 13 as per age of mother of deceased,

whereas,
multiplier has to be applied as per the age of deceased in light of catena of decisions of this Court as well as Apex Court. Further learned claims Tribunal erred in not awarding any amount under the head future prospects, whereas, in the light of decision of Apex Court in the matter of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors., (2017)16SCC680, since the deceased was self employed an addition of 40% of the established incomes should be required to be added.

sentences.text: Accordingly, while assessing the income of deceased Rs. 4,000/- per month

, his annual income comes to Rs. 48,000/- per annum to which  is required to be deducted towards personal expenses since deceased was unmarried and after deducting the same, remaining amount comes to Rs.
24,000/- to which 40% is required to be added towards future prospect and after adding the same,
amount comes to Rs. 33,600/- to which multiplier of 18 would be applicable and after applying the same, the amount under the head loss of dependency comes to Rs. 6,04,800/-.

Claimants shall also be entitled to receive a sum of Rs. 30,000/- under the heads funeral expenses and loss of estate and after adding the same, the total amount of compensation comes to Rs. 6,34,800/-.
The Claims Tribunal has already awarded a compensation of Rs. 3,42,000/-, therefore, claimants shall be entitled to receive an enhanced amount of compensation of Rs. 2,92,800/- .
The enhanced amount of compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim case.

10. As regards M.A.No. 5233/2019 moved on behalf of Insurance Company, from perusal of record,
it is clear that though Claims Tribunal found that offending vehicle was not possessing fitness certificate on the date of accident, however, ignored the same on the plea that no such condition of having fitness certificate in favour is mentioned in the insurance policy; whereas, this Court in the case of Vinod (supra) taking into consideration catena of decisions of this Court as well as Apex Court held that requirement of fitness certificate for liability of insurance company is not dependent upon terms and conditions of policy but it is the requirement of law, therefore, in the opinion of this Court, learned claims Tribunal erred in fastening the liability over the Insurance Company; whereas,
instead of Insurance Company, owner and driver of the offending vehicle are liable to be fastened with the liability.

However, in the light of decisions of Apex Court in the matter of Shivaraj Vs.
Rajendra [(2018) 10 SCC 432], Manuara Khatun Vs. Rajesh Kumar Singh [2017 ACJ 1031] &
Shamanna and another Vs. Divisional Manager, the Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. and others,[(2018)
9 SCC 650], Insurance Company is directed to make the payment of compensation amount first to the claimants with liberty to recover the same from the owner and driver of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: 11. Accordingly both the appeal are allowed in part and claimants are held entitled to receive enhanced compensation of Rs. 2,92,800/- which shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim case

Insurance Company is directed to make the payment of compensation amount first to the claimants within a period of two months from today with liberty to recover the same from the owner and driver of the offending vehicle.
12. Appeals stands disposed of.

(ROOPESH CHANDRA VARSHNEY) JUDGE jps/-
